description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities . Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the grant award letter, the dates for submission of the annual reports are mentioned. In case of a three-year project, between 5-7 reports are obligatory. The first report (0) is a very short report which focuses on specific conditions and/or recommendations in the grant. There is no need to report on progress in achieving outputs and outcomes, which is done in the first annual report. As annex to the report 0, the consortium agreements between the partners should be submitted. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

actual.value:
Our TMT project had foreseen four outputs:
- Increased capacities of MCIC and partners in managing multi-stakeholder processes & partnerships - Increased capacities of MCIC and partners program managers to manage programs results-based – through RBM - planning & RBM - monitoring and evaluation trainings - Increased capacities of MCIC and partners program managers in advocacy and policy influencing (API) - Increased capacities of MCIC and partners program managers in their training capacities
To achieve these outputs, we planned in the proposal five face to face trainings altogether.
_++**Set up of the trainings**++_
Due to COVID-19 pandemic we had to decide to deliver all trainings fully online. The trainings took place as follows:
- Stakeholder and partnership management training - 20 & 22 October + 3 & 5 November 2020 - Results-based management (RBM) - planning training - 17 & 19 Nov + 1 & 3 Dec 2020 - RBM - monitoring and evaluation - 16 & 18 + 23 & 25 March - Advocacy and policy influencing - 20 & 22 + 27 & 29 April - Training of Trainers - 21 & 31 May
On each training day we had two live plenary webinars - in the morning and in the afternoon. Participants worked in groups and on their cases, they had self-paced homework between the webinars during the day and also between the training weeks. First two trainings we implemented over the three weeks period, next two trainings over the two weeks period.
For Stakeholder and partnership management and Advocacy and policy influencing training we had participants from MCIC (requesting organisation) and from their partner organisations. In parallel to new learnings, participants created also further synergies working together, the cooperation continues after the training as their organisations work in the same regional networks in the area of rule of law, anticorruption and civil engagement in the Western Balkan region.
For RBM - planning, RBM - M&E and Training of Trainers trainings participants were all MCIC staff, the groups applied all tools and methodologies on MCIC three main programmes. The training triggered and inspired MCIC staff members to continue working on the programme results framework also after the trainings. The RBM planning and M&E trainings built up and followed up on each other.
_++**Participant's appreciation of the trainings**++_
As reported under _B.I.8. % alumni / TMT participants who state that they have acquired new knowledge and skills; e.g. problem solving, effective communication,_ 42 participants out of 44 who filled in the training end-evaluation surveys, indicated that they learned new skills and knowledge from the trainings. They highlighted many and variety of learning points in different trainings, and that is always a good sign for the trainers - all content of the trainings is relevant. The learnings are documented in the training end-evaluations.
All participants assessed the trainings also with the score of 'very good' (26) or 'good' (18). No one filled it in with 'fair' or 'poor'. Few quote examples from the participants per training are listed below:
- Participant's quote examples about the Stakeholder and partnership management training: '_Outstanding!'; 'Interactive, explanatory, networking, creating synergies, understanding each other.'; 'Useful training that everyone should go through at some point.'; 'Motivational, inspiring, new tools ... '_ - Participant's quote examples about the RBM - planning training:_ 'Excellent, go for it!'; 'Interesting and useful'_ - Participant's quote examples about RBM - M&E training: _'One of the most relatable courses that I had within MCIC. Very useful and practical.'; 'The way of thinking that contributes and influence not only ones working logic but something that can be used in everyday life'; 'Well structured, adapted for distant learning, highly interactive.'; 'Not for everyone.'_ - Participant's quote examples about Advocacy and policy influencing training: '_This course provides all the essentials on advocacy and policy influencing. It is a backbone necessary for the understanding and improvement of your advocacy and policy strategies.'; 'The course offers a valuable knowledge that can be applied in our work, even though we are not all necessarily involved in advocacy.'_ - Participant's quote examples about Training of Trainers training: _'Useful for daily work, great trainings methods used during the actual training implementation'; 'The course is very useful for anyone engaging with public relations and wishing to present findings, stories, ideas to the peers and wider public'._
_++**Milestones beyond trainings**++_
First of all, we are proud that all trainings resulted in discussions and recommendations that triggered also more strategic questions for MCIC (the requesting organisation) to discuss further and eventually answer. To anchor the discussions properly, we decided jointly to organise extra two days special strategic workshop for MCIC staff and reflect and collect all strategic questions relevant for MCIC to answer within their new organisational strategy. Few examples of the critical questions for MCIC to answer, were:
- MCIC on the cross roads: which **role** (to continue) to take? What will be your priority focus? Do you need to take (even) more activist role and / or be the broker to bring movement btw. government and CSOs and citizens real needs? Being dependent on funding from government and / or donors again, can downsize this ambition. - What are the critical key signs for MCIC to measure? - Who is / are our constituencies we represent?
Secondly, through continuous contact and follow-up, staff members and management informed us that they have practised with the tools and methods from the trainings also beyond the trainings. In every training we applied the tools on actual programmes. For example as a result of API and RBM - planning and M&E trainings, participants had developed products such as API strategies, M&E frameworks, programme results chains, indicators that they continued to use in practice after trainings. Participants appreciated it very much!
A third and last additional complementary element, we introduced to MCIC and it's strategic discussion, were the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Through a special certified SDG Game and MDF facilitator, Sam Boering, we increased awareness among MCIC staff how SDGs can affect MCIC strategic future.

comment.narrative:
10-08-2022: - Stakeholder and partnership management training, nine organisatons: MCIC, CAFT, CCC, CRNVO, BCSDN, IDSCS, Konekt, European Western Balkans, Institut Alternativa - Results-based management - planning training, one organisation: MCIC - Results-based management - M&E, one organisation: MCIC - Advocacy and policy influencing, eight organisations: MCIC, CAFT, CCC, CRNVO, BCSDN, IDSCS, Konekt, European Western Balkans - Sustainable Development Goals workshop one organisation: MCIC - Training of trainers training, one organisation: MCIC - MCIC strategy workshop, one organisation: MCIC
All organisations are non-government and / or civil society organisations.
4 out of 21 participants, filling in our end alumni survey, have stated that they have been able to introduce new tools and methods to their partners in their regional cooperation network members who did not participate in any of the trainings already. 18 people confirmed also that they plan (to continue) to do so in the future.
